articles.title: Smile arrives at Europe’s Spaceport
articles.summary: The Smile spacecraft has arrived at Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana. During the coming weeks, the spacecraft will go through final preparations for its launch on a Vega-C rocket between 8 April and 7 May.

articles.title: ESA analysing fireball over Europe on 8 March 2026
articles.summary: At approximately 18:55 CET (17:55 UTC) on Sunday 8 March 2026, a very bright fireball moving from the southwest to the northeast was observed by many people in Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands.

articles.title: "She flies satellites. One day, I can too."
articles.summary: At ESA’s European Space Operations Centre (ESOC), teams work around the clock to fly spacecraft across the Solar System and monitor Earth from orbit. Among them are women leading spacecraft operations, managing teams and helping shape the culture of ESA’s mission control.

articles.title: Hostage to the Moon - How Artemis Became Industrial Welfare in a Space Suit - Part 2
articles.summary:
Los Angeles CA (SPX) Mar 09, 2026

NASA says it has finally found the "back to basics" recipe to get Americans back on the Moon by 2028. A new intermediate mission, standardized hardware, a faster launch cadence: on paper, the Artemis overhaul looks like a sober course correction after years of drift.
